primary.title: Elements
primary.author: Euclid
primary.rationale: Euclid's seminal work on geometry, foundational to mathematics. It exists in numerous translations and editions.

secondary.title: Euclid's Elements
secondary.author: Euclid
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive translation and commentary on Euclid's Elements by Thomas L. Heath, considered a standard scholarly edition.

secondary.title: The Crest of the Peacock: Non-European Roots of Mathematics
secondary.author: George Gheverghese Joseph
secondary.rationale: This book discusses the historical development of mathematics, including Euclid's contributions within a broader global context.

secondary.title: Euclid's Window: The Story of Geometry from Parallel Lines to Hyperspace
secondary.author: Leonard Mlodinow
secondary.rationale: A popular science book that explores the history and concepts of geometry, with significant focus on Euclid and his work.

suggestions.notes: Euclid's primary work, 'Elements', is the most significant primary source. Secondary sources focus on scholarly analysis and historical context of his work.
